text:
sam: Quick thought: add a fallback hysteresis score so we don't flip on marginal signals. Instead of binary trigger, compute confidence and require it to exceed a threshold for T seconds.
liv: That feels sensible. Confidence could aggregate error_ratio, p95, and recent fallback history.
ben: Keep API simple: confidence_threshold and sustain_ms. Default 0.75, sustain 10s.
ops-bot: [alert] 4395007765 - policy p-900 evaluated CONFIDENCE=0.62 (below 0.75) -> deferred :information_source:
telemetry-bot: emit CONFIDENCE_EVAL events with fields: policy_id, confidence, window_ms, contributing_signals (CSV).
liv: UX: show a small confidence bar in timeline and an orange "watch" state while below threshold. Hover lists contributing signals and weights.
sam: Server-side: derive confidence via weighted sum; weights visible in advanced UI. Prevent weights >1 sum without warning.
ben: Also add operator override to force fallback; log OVERRIDE_FALLBACK with user and reason.
ops-bot: [note] 4395007795 - operator @liv forced fallback p-900 due to customer impact :warning:
sam: Tests: run 100 spike sims and compare oscillation count with/without confidence hysteresis. Ben, can you add to the harness?
ben: Yep, will add weighted confidence mode and a comparison metric.
liv: I'll draft the console mock and tooltip copy: "Confidence hysteresis: require sustained high-confidence to trigger fallback, reducing false positives."
sam: Good. We'll gate behind feature flag and tune defaults per deployment tier.
__note: Slack thread as a single continuous string with messages prefixed by sender names. All top-level values are strings or list of strings as required.
